column1: # Y-STR panel of step 45: the 111 markers of FamilyTreeDNA's Y-111 test, in FamilyTreeDNA's order.
# Sources, read 2026-10-25:
#   order, names and panels: FamilyTreeDNA Help Center, "Y-STR Results Guide",
#     https://help.familytreedna.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408063356303-Y-STR-Results-Guide
#     (the live page refuses scripted requests; read through the Internet Archive copy of 2026-04-13,
#     https://web.archive.org/web/20260413211616/https://help.familytreedna.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408063356303-Y-STR-Results-Guide;
#     its Panel 3 list prints DYS456 twice, the twelve loci 26-37 are as below)
#   regions (GRCh38, 1-based, inclusive), motif length and reference copies: HipSTR-references
#     human/all_annot_markers.hg38.fixed.bed at commit cc9275210a10911721015ce908f30a12e4ea44ca (MIT),
#     https://github.com/HipSTR-Tool/HipSTR-references/blob/cc9275210a10911721015ce908f30a12e4ea44ca/human/all_annot_markers.hg38.fixed.bed
#     sha256 d5b91757c7de756ada8a940cb5588e6f51aa79513ae6ce8cb4f1b9df63df9e61; the Y-STR marker set of
#     Willems et al. 2016 (PMID 27126583) and HipSTR (Willems et al. 2017, PMID 28436466)
#   motif: NIST STRBase repeat structure, https://strbase.nist.gov/api/loci (seqPattern)
# Columns:
#   order    position in FamilyTreeDNA's list (1-111)
#   panel    the smallest FamilyTreeDNA test that has the marker (Y-12, Y-25, Y-37, Y-67, Y-111)
#   marker   FamilyTreeDNA's name; the copies of a multi-copy marker are a, b, c, d
#   kind     single    one HipSTR region
#            parts     several HipSTR regions of one locus; the count is their sum
#            multicopy the repeat lies in two or more copies of duplicated (palindromic) Y sequence:
#                      short reads cannot tell the copies apart, so it is not called
#            absent    no region for it in the HipSTR marker set, so it is not called
#   regions  chrom:start-end/motif length/reference copies/HipSTR name, ';' between parts; '.' when none
#   motif    STRBase repeat structure, '.' when STRBase has none
#   offset   whole repeats to add to reach FamilyTreeDNA's count; '.' when no published value was found
#            (none was, for any marker, on 2026-10-25: see docs/45-y-str.md)
#   note     what the count covers, '.' for nothing to add
order

column8: FamilyTreeDNA reports DYS389II as the sum total of DYS389I and DYS389II; the two regions span the whole locus (DYS389II.1 starts where DYS389I starts), so this count covers DYS389I too
